label: early copy phase (<DEL> through recall of original token 3), content-gated
explanation: Almost silent in the original phase (0.3% of mass). Fires at the <DEL> step and the first few copy steps: rate peaks at recall_idx 2 (20%), and recall_idx 0-3 holds about 88% of mass. Rate rises with L (L=9 is 1.3x). Inside this window only about 14-20% of steps fire, and which ones depends on content. It favors sequences containing h or i, with active runs that usually start at <DEL> and continue until an h/i (or i/l/x/o/d) is about to be output. Inputs h/i have 3-4x lift, and next_out i has 4.8x lift. Sequences with no h/i in the early part rarely fire. Predicates that capture this content gating (an h/i coming up within the next few outputs) raise precision only to about 0.24 and cost about half the recall, so the content rule is not clean. The predicate gives the positional envelope only: high mass recall, low precision.
